question:
Adjusters must be able to ask natural-language coverage questions and receive answers grounded strictly in Caeldyne's current policy documents, with no fabricated coverage terms.

Which three actions should the team take? (Select three.)

options.text: Ingest the policy PDFs and run OCR/layout enrichment so their text and clause structure are captured before indexing.
Build a vector index over the policy content, chunked at a level that preserves individual coverage clauses.
Configure the agent's retrieval tool to cite the retrieved passages so answers can be traced back to specific policy language.
Skip indexing entirely and paste the full text of every policy PDF into the model's context window on every question.
Fine-tune a new base model on the wording of the current policies so it memorizes coverage terms.

explanation:
A grounded RAG pipeline needs all three: **enrichment/OCR** so the retrievable text is complete and structured, **clause-aware chunking with vector indexing** so retrieval returns the specific relevant passage instead of an entire document, and **citations back to source passages** so an adjuster (and an auditor) can verify the answer isn't fabricated.

**Why not the other options:**
- **Pasting every policy into context every time** — Doesn't scale, wastes tokens on irrelevant policies for a given question, and provides no retrieval ranking — it is not RAG, just a brute-force context stuff that will fail once the policy library grows.
- **Fine-tuning on policy wording** — Fine-tuning nudges style and tone; it does not reliably encode exact, current, and updatable factual clauses, and policies change over time. It does not provide traceable citations and is a known path to *more* fabrication risk, not less, since the model can blend memorized wording with hallucinated wording.
